newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Energy Africa to get most Gabon oil rights.
newsitem.headline: Energy Africa to get most Gabon oil rights.

text.p: South African oil company Energy Africa Ltd said on Wednesday it will acquire the right to participate in six potential development projects and 22 exploration projects in Gabon.

It said in a statement, the acreage covered by these rights includes substantially all the exploration licences currently in effect in Gabon and in excess of 80 percent of the onshore and offshore sedimentary basin of the African country.

John Bentley, Energy Africa's managing director, declined to pin a price to the deal, but said the cost of the acquisition and projected development costs could readily be met from its existing cash resources.
"The various licences which we have access to cover most of the prospective area in the country," Bentley told Reuters on Wednesday.

Wednesday's more detailed release follows an announcement on Monday that the South African firm had entered into a partnership agreement with the Republic of Gabon to participate in exploration and development projects there.

The statement said the Gabonese rights would be held by Energy Africa Gabon SA (EAG SA), which would be owned 25 percent by Gabon and 75 percent by a joint venture company. The latter will be 50 percent held by Energy Africa and 50 by an African investment group.

"This transaction will ensure that Energy Africa has exposure to most exploration successes in Gabon and the deep-water licenses in particular hold considerable potential," Bentley said, adding that it would put EAG SA in a strong position to pursue further opportunities.
The rights to be acquired by EAG SA under the deal are:
* A 40 percent stake in three satellites to the onshore Rabi Kounga field, namely Niungo, Moukouti and Ganga. These are operated by Kelt Gabon and are the subject of development feasibility studies.

* Interests of 20 percent in Ablette, 20 percent in Limande and 27.5 percent in Turnix which are three offshore discoveries also the subject of development studies. Limande is operated by Agip Gabon and the other two by Kelt Gabon.
* The option to acquire interests of differing sizes, in the event of a discovery being made, in 22 other contracts currently being undertaken by a number of international operators.
Energy Africa said it had undertaken to provide technical assistance to Gabon in monitoring the progress of these projects.
It said the agreement was initiated last November at the time of the state visit to South Africa of Gabon President El Hadj Omar Bongo. Bentley said it was finalised over the weekend.
Energy Africa is already involved in oil activities throughout Africa, including exploration in Angola, and production operations offshore Congo.
